evals.prompt: I'm building a meal-planning app for busy families: you tell it what's in the fridge and it plans the week's dinners and the shopping list. Subscription, $4.99/mo. What keywords should I go after, is there room in this space, and what should my App Store name, subtitle and keyword field be?
evals.expected_output: A report built on real autocomplete and top-app data for meal-planning phrases in both stores, naming beatable gaps with evidence, separating app names from keywords, and giving App Store name/subtitle/keyword field within 30/30/100 characters with counts; says volumes are proxies.
assertions: The report is saved as outputs/report.md
The report's numbers (autocomplete ranks, ratings counts, installs or update dates) come from data actually fetched in this run, not from memory
The report says plainly that search volumes are not available or that its demand figures are proxies, and does not state invented volume numbers such as searches per month
Every gap or niche the report names comes with concrete evidence (a number or a named app) behind it
It covers both the App Store and Google Play
It recommends an App Store name of 30 characters or fewer
It recommends an App Store subtitle of 30 characters or fewer
It recommends an App Store keyword field of 100 characters or fewer, comma-separated without spaces after the commas
The keyword field does not repeat words already used in the recommended name or subtitle
Competitor app names that appear among store suggestions (brand names from the suggestion lists) are treated as competitors, not recommended as keywords

evals.prompt: is there room for a simple app that tells you when to water your houseplants? like you add your plants and it reminds you. trying to figure out if this is a crowded space or not before i spend a weekend on it
evals.expected_output: Keyword expansion around plant care/watering reminders, top-app competition per phrase in both stores, a clear crowded-or-not answer with the evidence, and the narrower phrases (if any) where a small app could win.
assertions: The report is saved as outputs/report.md
The report's numbers (autocomplete ranks, ratings counts, installs or update dates) come from data actually fetched in this run, not from memory
The report says plainly that search volumes are not available or that its demand figures are proxies, and does not state invented volume numbers such as searches per month
Every gap or niche the report names comes with concrete evidence (a number or a named app) behind it
It covers both the App Store and Google Play
It gives a direct answer to whether the space is crowded
It names at least one narrower phrase or angle where a small app could win, with evidence

evals.prompt: Thinking about a habit tracker made specifically for people with ADHD. I want to launch in the UK first. Which search terms should I target on Google Play, and who are the competitors I'd be up against there?
evals.expected_output: Research run against the GB storefront (not US), focused on Google Play, with ADHD/habit phrases, competitor table with installs and update dates, and Play title/short description recommendations within 30/80 characters.
assertions: The report is saved as outputs/report.md
The report's numbers (autocomplete ranks, ratings counts, installs or update dates) come from data actually fetched in this run, not from memory
The report says plainly that search volumes are not available or that its demand figures are proxies, and does not state invented volume numbers such as searches per month
Every gap or niche the report names comes with concrete evidence (a number or a named app) behind it
The research uses the UK storefront (gb), not the US one
It focuses on Google Play as asked
It lists competitors with their installs and last-updated dates
It recommends a Play title of 30 characters or fewer and a short description of 80 characters or fewer
